title: Bug: %/% tokenized as two tokens (Mod + SlashPercent) instead of one
description: Lexer bug in parser.rs: the integer division operator %/% is broken. When the lexer encounters %, it peeks forward and sees / (not %), so it emits Token::Mod (%%). Then / is consumed, peeks %, emits Token::SlashPercent. Result: a %/% b is lexed as [Mod, SlashPercent] and parsed as a %% / b. Fix: in the '%' branch, check for /% as a 3-character sequence before checking for %%.
close_reason: Closed

title: Complete bc_eval.rs: ~67% of opcodes unimplemented

Without these, no compiled R package code runs.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix arithmetic.rs: vectorize all operations (scalar-only is wrong)
description: arithmetic.rs only handles scalar SEXP values. real_val() reads element [0] via *data. Every arithmetic op silently produces wrong results on vectors. In R, + is vectorized: c(1,2,3)+c(4,5,6) must produce c(5,6,7) with recycling. The C source (arithmetic.c:527) dispatches to R_binary() which handles integer_binary() and real_binary() with full vectorization and recycling. Missing: R_binary(), integer_binary(), real_binary(), logical/integer/real unary ops, integer overflow -> NA_integer_ semantics, do_math2/math3/math4, do_log/do_log_builtin.
close_reason: Closed

title: SEXP free_node can be revisited by GC and double-free payload
description:
Why: memory.rs free_node deallocates payload and pushes node onto free_list, but arena.nodes() still iterates those nodes and later GC passes can revisit/free stale payload state. This risks double-free/use-after-free behavior in GC paths.

What: ensure freed nodes are excluded from GC scans or have their payload/generation/mark state cleared so repeated reclamation is impossible. Add a regression test that frees and then runs repeated GC cycles.

Done: repeated GC cycles do not attempt to reclaim already-freed node payloads; regression test passes.
notes: Implemented in commit 8488b55. RArena::free_node is now idempotent (returns early if pointer already in free_list), and freed nodes are tombstoned: gengc_next_node cleared, attrib cleared, mark cleared, and generation set to Old to avoid repeated young-collection free attempts. Added regression coverage: sexp::memory::tests::test_arena_free_node_idempotent, test_arena_free_vector_clears_payload_pointer, and sexp::gengc::tests::test_minor_gc_does_not_refree_nodes_on_free_list. Validation: cargo test -p rmath sexp::memory::tests::test_arena_free_node_idempotent -- --exact; cargo test -p rmath sexp::memory::tests::test_arena_free_vector_clears_payload_pointer -- --exact; cargo test -p rmath sexp::gengc::tests::test_minor_gc_does_not_refree_nodes_on_free_list -- --exact.
close_reason: Closed

title: SEXP GC compaction treats atomic vectors as SEXP pointers
description:
Why: full GC compaction in gengc.rs currently casts vector payloads to SEXP* for all vector SEXPTYPEs. This is only valid for pointer vectors (VECSXP/EXPRSXP/STRSXP), but is UB for atomic vectors (INTSXP/REALSXP/LGLSXP/CPLXSXP/RAWSXP) and can corrupt memory during reference updates.

What: split compaction/update logic by payload kind and only walk pointer-bearing vectors as SEXP references. Atomic vectors should be copied/compacted as opaque bytes without per-element pointer rewriting. Add regression tests that compact each vector kind.

Done: compaction no longer reinterprets atomic payloads as SEXP pointers; tests cover vector-type-specific compaction behavior and pass.
notes: Implemented in commit 09576fa. GC reference-rewrite phases in sexp/gengc.rs now only walk pointer-bearing vector payloads (STRSXP/VECSXP/EXPRSXP) via vector_payload_has_sexp_refs(), instead of all is_vector_type() payloads. This removes UB reinterpretation of atomic payloads as SEXP*. Added regression tests: test_update_object_references_skips_atomic_vector_payloads (REALSXP payload bit-pattern remains unchanged even when matching a mapped old pointer) and test_update_object_references_updates_pointer_vector_payloads (VECSXP payload is correctly rewritten). Validation: cargo test -p rmath sexp::gengc::tests::test_update_object_references_skips_atomic_vector_payloads -- --exact; cargo test -p rmath sexp::gengc::tests::test_update_object_references_updates_pointer_vector_payloads -- --exact.
close_reason: Closed

title: Protection stack APIs fail open on allocation failure
description:
Why: protect.rs currently swallows try_reserve failures in Rf_protect/R_ProtectWithIndex/R_PreserveObject. Calls appear successful even when values were not protected, creating latent GC safety bugs.

What: make protection APIs fail closed (explicit error or status) when stack growth fails, and align index-return behavior so callers cannot receive a bogus sentinel that looks valid. Add tests for simulated allocation failure paths.

Done: failed protection allocation is surfaced explicitly and never reports success; tests cover failure semantics.
notes: Implemented fail-closed semantics for protection stack allocation in commit 0cdbebd. Rf_protect, R_ProtectWithIndex, and R_PreserveObject now route through reserve_slot_or_fail and panic on reserve failure instead of silently succeeding. Added test-only reserve-failure hook plus regression tests: sexp::protect::tests::test_protect_reserve_failure_panics, test_protect_with_index_reserve_failure_panics, and test_preserve_reserve_failure_panics. Also corrected protect_n documentation to reflect actual RAII semantics (unprotect guard over pre-protected entries).
close_reason: Closed
